fields.hero_prompt: Build a dermaplaning consent form for my mobile facial business that clients sign on their phone, with a skin history section.

faq_plan.q: What is a dermaplaning consent form?
How do I create a dermaplaning consent form?

plan.angle: The top 10 is printable dermaplaning consent PDFs and fill-and-sign templates (spa practice forms, a forms bundle, PDF editors, two form-builder templates): one sheet, signed once, filed. This page shows the form as an app a skin practice runs: a dermaplaning section that opens only when a client adds it to a facial, links signed before a mobile esthetician leaves home, a skin history yes that holds the booking for review without sending the answers in the alert, and student treatments countersigned by the instructor. The consent wording stays with the practice's provider or lawyer; the page makes no claim about dermaplaning risks, contraindications, who may perform it or whether a signature makes consent valid, and quotes MedlinePlus only for what written informed consent is.
tab_stories: Jovana Enright books a hydrating facial at Velvetleaf Skin Studio and adds dermaplaning; her consent link opens the facial terms plus 4 dermaplaning statements to initial, and her record reads facial and dermaplaning signed.
Ingrith Ivanska of Glowcart Mobile Facials emails each client a consent link with the booking; on Saturday morning her screen shows all 5 clients signed before she loads the car.

Tullia Kestrova answers yes to 1 skin history question at Gildenrow Aesthetics; her booking is marked needs review, and Desmonda Rosewarne gets an email that a form needs review with a link, never the answer itself.

At Treharne School of Esthetics, student Birgitta performs each dermaplaning treatment and instructor Ragnhild countersigns the form; by Friday 11 of 12 student treatments are countersigned and 1 waits on her list.
